Samira — appreciate the clear profile. Looping Marissa (fleet lead) and Lauren (sales ops) to draft a policy you can drop into the SOW. High level answers up front: 

- Billing: reserved capacity covers baseline GPUs; burst is metered by GPU-minute at a premium multiplier. We can add a monthly burst cap and alerting hooks.
- Throttle: yes — we can set a hard throttle and a soft-burst window (configurable). Soft bursts allow up to 2.5x for 2–5 minutes before throttling to 2x sustained.
- Warmup: typical cold-start to steady-state p95 is ~12–35s depending on model KV cache reuse; for our recommended config (prefix caching + pre-warm threads) median is ~18s.

Action plan: Marissa will propose a precise autoscale spec (rules, cooldowns, headroom multipliers) and a one-paragraph SLA snippet. Lauren will add the burst cap clause to the commercial term sheet draft.

Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Samira, Rishi — attached a concise autoscale runbook and an SLA paragraph draft (see autoscale-runbook.txt and redwood_sla-draft.pdf). TL;DR from infra: 

- Policy model: baseline reserved slab (configurable GPUs), soft-burst window (configurable duration T_soft), and hard-throttle cap. We recommend default: T_soft = 180s, soft_headroom = 2.5x, hard_cap = 2.0x sustained (30s smoothing).
- Billing guardrail: implement a monthly burst-spend cap at account level; once reached, either auto-throttle to baseline or fail fast depending on customer choice.
- Pre-warm options: scheduled pre-warm for predictable releases (cron), and API-driven pre-warm hooks for traffic-based signals. Pre-warm reduces warmup p95 by ~10–15s in our tests.
- Observability: token-level CPU/GPU breakdown, per-route cost, and alerting thresholds for both spend and latency.

Open items for commercial/legal: 
- Exact premium for burst GPU-minute: default 1.8x of reserved rate; negotiable on committed spend.
- Definition of "sustained" for hard_cap enforcement (we use 30s smoothed avg; can be extended).

Next steps: Lauren, can you draft the billing cap language + an example monthly cap table for ZEN-483? Samira — if you prefer a fail-fast model when the cap hits, say so and we'll include the option in the SOW.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, GPU Fleet — Redwood Inference

Attachments: autoscale-runbook.txt (plain text, 6KB), redwood_sla-draft.pdf (pdf, 18KB)

Marissa / team — this is exactly what we needed, thank you. A couple quick notes from infra and procurement: 

- Procurement wants a monthly burst cap with a notification at 80% and automatic throttle-to-baseline at 100%. They prefer fail-fast only for non-critical routes.
- We accept the 1.8x burst premium for pilot months; procurement will request a step-down to 1.5x at 12-month commit if we hit forecasted usage.
- For warmup: we will use API-driven pre-warm calls around launches and a small scheduled warm pool for auth-heavy flows.

Please attach the SOW snippet and the billing-cap clause to the HubSpot deal and share a DocuSign link for the SLA so procurement can sign. We'll also need a short checklist for on-call escalation during the first 3 months of GA.
